section.title: High-Level Architecture
section.description: - Section 4 answers which system boundaries and constraints a regenerated implementation must preserve. - It does NOT inventory technologies that a developer can recover from code or dependency metadata. Frameworks, SDKs, ORMs, internal database products, credential wiring, and CI tools remain implementation discretion unless a product, contract, regulation, or external boundary mandates the choice. - Section 4.1 shows the product and major runtime/data boundaries once. Section 4.2 records only durable architecture constraints. Section 7.3 explains how one Feature crosses the approved boundaries without re-declaring implementation technology. - `/feature-to-adr` later transfers durable contracts and boundaries into ADRs and leaves replaceable technology means to code. After successful handoff, ADRs are the implementation authority and this Section remains legacy planning context.

subsection.title: System Diagram
subsection.description: - Provide both a Context diagram and a Container diagram using Mermaid C4 syntax. - The Context diagram is required. Show the people, external systems, the target system, and their relationships. - The Container diagram is required. Show the major independently running or deployable applications and data stores inside the target system, their responsibilities, durable boundaries, and relationships. - These are the only C4 levels allowed in an ALPS PRD. Do not generate Component, Dynamic, Deployment, or Code-level C4 diagrams. - Keep modules, classes, functions, files, methods, libraries, frameworks, and other implementation details out of both diagrams.
subsection.example:
```mermaid C4Context
title System Context Diagram for Document Assistant
Person(author, "Document Author", "Creates a product document through conversation") System(documentAssistant, "Document Assistant", "Guides the author and produces the document") System_Ext(llm, "LLM Service", "Generates guided questions and draft content")
Rel(author, documentAssistant, "Authors a document with") Rel(documentAssistant, llm, "Requests language generation from") ```
```mermaid C4Container
title Container Diagram for Document Assistant
Person(author, "Document Author", "Creates a product document through conversation") System_Ext(llm, "LLM Service", "Generates guided questions and draft content")
System_Boundary(documentAssistant, "Document Assistant") { Container(webApp, "Web Application", "Web UI", "Runs the guided authoring conversation") Container(api, "Application API", "Server application", "Manages the authoring workflow and document state") ContainerDb(documentStore, "Document Store", "Persistent storage", "Stores approved product documents") }
Rel(author, webApp, "Uses") Rel(webApp, api, "Sends approved section content to") Rel(api, documentStore, "Reads and writes") Rel(api, llm, "Requests language generation from") ```

subsection.title: Architecture Constraints
subsection.description: - Record only conditions a regenerated implementation must preserve: - Scale assumption: expected total and concurrent usage when it constrains the product or an NFR. - Access boundary: required user channels such as browser, mobile, or both. - Mandated platform or external provider: only when a contract, regulation, organization policy, or durable system boundary requires it. - Data and security boundary: residency, isolation, trust, encryption, or privacy constraints. - Deployment boundary: required regions, environments, availability, recovery, or offline constraints. - State the requirement and its basis. Do not list a technology merely because it is the current or recommended implementation. - Exclude replaceable frameworks, SDKs, ORMs, internal database products, credential plumbing, module layouts, CI tools, and tuning values. Code and dependency metadata own those facts. - If no additional durable constraints exist beyond Section 4.1, state that directly instead of inventing a technology recommendation.
subsection.example: - Scale assumption: ~1,000 total users at launch, tens concurrent at peak - Access boundary: users access the MVP through a web browser. - Data boundary: customer documents remain in the contracted region. - External provider boundary: the model provider must satisfy the organization's no-training data policy.
